historical_eic_review.method: Independent public-source research, not execution of product code or tests. Parse $50 EIC rows from archived IRS instructions and compare every numeric cell with decimal half-up arithmetic. Starred terminal cells are excluded from the full-band counts; all eight terminal footnotes per year were separately extracted, reconciled with decimal midpoint arithmetic, and transcribed into regressions. No claim is made for unparsed rows.
historical_eic_review.maximum_rounding: 2021–2023 retain creditRate * earnedIncomeAmount before subtracting phaseout, including terminal bands. The 2024 table uses rounded maxCredit for both full and terminal bands. Applying unrounded maximum to 2024 full bands causes 454 differences; rounded maximum causes zero differences in the parsed cells. All 32 historical terminal footnotes agree with these annual conventions. The existing 2025/2026 profile remains unchanged: rounded full-band maximum, unrounded terminal-band maximum.
historical_eic_review.terminal_rounding_example: 2024 nonjoint/no-child $18,550–$18,591 uses midpoint 18570.5: rounded maximum 632 minus 0.0765 * (18570.5 - 10330) = 1.60175, rounding to the printed $2. Unrounded maximum 631.89 would incorrectly yield $1. Nonjoint/one-child $49,050–$49,084 similarly yields the printed $3 with rounded maximum 4213, rather than $2 with unrounded maximum 4212.6.
